key_insight: The paper shows that the complete electrode model for EIT can be implemented using standard Robin boundary conditions, while preserving equivalence to the conventional current-driven formulation.
engineering_relevance: This makes highly accurate electrode voltage prediction portable across common FEM packages without requiring specialized CEM boundary machinery.
method: Use prescribed electrode-potential Robin problems to compute unit-potential responses.
Assemble an electrode transadmittance matrix and enforce current constraints through a small electrode system.
Prove discrete equivalence to the augmented CEM and verify the implementation across multiple FEM codes.
evidence_signal: Across five FEM packages, electrode-potential differences from EIDORS stayed below 5×10^-13, and errors versus an exact rational-arithmetic reference were below 1.1×10^-13.
watch_item: The equivalence relies on the Robin matrix being invertible, so implementations must ensure this condition and consistent reference-potential handling.
paper_title: Implementing the EIT complete electrode model through Robin boundary conditions
